summary: Specifies Cisco's Hot Standby Router Protocol, which lets hosts appear to use a single router and keep connectivity even if the actual first-hop router fails. It is informational and documents a vendor protocol.

eli5.summary: Two routers share one pretend identity. If the main one breaks, the spare takes over and you do not notice.

questions: how does hot standby router protocol work
how does hsrp elect the active router
what is the hsrp virtual mac address
subtitle: How a group of routers shares one virtual router address so hosts keep working when the first-hop router fails.

tldr.problem: Many hosts can only be configured with one default router and cannot discover another, so if that router fails they lose connectivity.
tldr.mechanism: Routers form a standby group that acts as one virtual router with a virtual IP and MAC address. One active router forwards packets, one standby router waits, and they elect each other with Hello, Coup and Resign messages sent over UDP port 1985.
tldr.outcome: If the active router fails, the standby takes over without a major interruption for hosts. The protocol offers no real security, only a clear-text password.

today: RFC 2281 is an Informational memo from March 1998 and is not obsoleted or updated by any other RFC. Its IESG note says it reflects an existing deployed protocol while an IETF working group was producing a standards track protocol for the same issues.

sections.title: The Hot Standby Router Protocol
sections.content:
HSRP is a Cisco protocol, documented here as an existing deployed protocol, that supports non-disruptive failover of IP traffic when a host cannot learn its first-hop router dynamically. It is designed for multi-access, multicast or broadcast capable LANs such as Ethernet. It is not meant to replace dynamic router discovery, which should be used whenever possible.

A set of routers, the standby group, presents the illusion of a single virtual router. One active router forwards the packets hosts send to it, and one standby router is ready to replace it. After the election, only these two send periodic messages. Several groups can coexist on a LAN, and splitting hosts among groups gives load splitting. Each group has one well-known MAC address and one IP address, which SHOULD be on the LAN's primary subnet but MUST differ from every interface address on the LAN.

The memo also states that a Cisco patent may apply, which Cisco will license on reasonable, nondiscriminatory terms.
sections.eli5: Imagine a school door with one name on it, but two teachers who can staff it. One teaches while the other waits, and if the first leaves, the second steps in with the same name tag.

sections.title: HSRP Packets
sections.content:
HSRP runs over UDP port 1985, sending to multicast address 224.0.0.2 with TTL 1. Routers use their real IP address as the source, not the virtual one, so peers can identify each other.

The message has fields for version (0 in this document), op code, state, hellotime, holdtime, priority, group, 8 octets of authentication data and the 4-octet virtual IP address. Op codes are Hello (0), Coup (1) and Resign (2). A Hello says a router is running and could be active or standby, a Coup says it wants to become active, and a Resign says it no longer wants to be active.

The Hellotime defaults to 3 seconds (RECOMMENDED) and the Holdtime to 10 seconds. The Holdtime SHOULD be at least three times the Hellotime. Priority elects the routers: the higher number wins, and equal priorities are decided by the higher IP address. The authentication data is a clear-text 8 character password.
sections.eli5: The routers pass little notes that say who they are, how important they are, and a shared password.

sections.title: States, Timers and Events
sections.content:
Each router runs a state machine with six states: Initial, Learn, Listen, Speak, Standby and Active. Initial means HSRP is not running. Learn means the router does not yet know the virtual IP address. Listen means it knows it but is neither active nor standby. Speak means it sends Hellos and takes part in the election. Excluding transient conditions, at most one router is in Standby and at most one in Active.

Three timers are kept: an Active timer and a Standby timer, which watch the other routers and are set to the Holdtime from their Hello, and a Hello timer that fires once per Hellotime and MUST be jittered. A router configured to preempt that has higher priority than the active router can take over by sending a Coup.

The memo gives a table of transitions for events such as timer expiry and receipt of Hello, Coup or Resign messages. When a router becomes active it sends a gratuitous ARP response advertising the virtual IP and virtual MAC address.
sections.eli5: Each router goes from waiting, to listening, to speaking up, to being the spare, to being the boss. Alarm clocks tell it if the boss or spare has gone quiet.

sections.title: Virtual MAC Addresses
sections.content:
Each group has a well-known virtual MAC address. On media other than Token Ring it is 0x00 0x00 0x0C 0x07 0xAC XX, where XX is the group number. The active router MUST accept and forward traffic sent to it and stop when it leaves the Active state, and it uses that address as the source of its Hello messages so learning bridges can follow it. Hosts therefore never need to change their ARP entries when the active router changes.

Some hardware can filter only one unicast MAC address, in which case the router must change its primary MAC address when it becomes active, and some protocols such as DECnet phase IV may not be able to run alongside HSRP. Using a router's normal MAC address as the virtual one is allowed but strongly discouraged.

Routers in HSRP MUST NOT send ICMP redirects on the interface, so hosts do not learn real router addresses. If proxy ARP is supported, replies MUST carry the virtual MAC address and MUST NOT be suppressed because of HSRP state.
sections.eli5: Everyone on the street sends mail to the same pretend address, so when the teacher on duty changes, nobody needs a new address book.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The memo says plainly that the protocol does not provide security. The authentication field is only useful for preventing misconfiguration. An active intruder on the LAN can easily subvert it, causing a packet black hole and a denial-of-service attack. Subverting it from outside the LAN is hard, as most routers will not forward packets addressed to 224.0.0.2.
sections.eli5: The password is like a note anyone nearby can read, so it stops mistakes but not a determined troublemaker on the same network.

fields.name: Version
fields.desc: Version of the HSRP messages; this document describes version 0.

fields.name: State
fields.desc: Current state of the sending router.

fields.name: Holdtime
fields.desc: Seconds a Hello message is considered valid.

fields.desc: Used to elect the active and standby routers.

fields.desc: Virtual IP address used by this group.

items.label: Learn
items.desc: Virtual IP address not yet known.

items.label: Listen
items.desc: Knows the virtual IP; neither active nor standby.

items.label: Speak
items.desc: Sends Hellos and takes part in the election.

items.label: Standby
items.desc: Candidate to become the next active router.

items.label: Active
items.desc: Forwards packets sent to the virtual MAC address.
